title: Microsoft Purview retention: what is kept, what is deleted and who decides
summary: The page leaves AI-app retention pricing as an open question although Microsoft publishes a rate. Three control paths also stop at the entrance to a wizard, omitting the policy-type choice and location selector needed to configure the control described.

claims.claim: Purview retention policies and labels determine how long Microsoft 365 content, including Copilot interactions, is retained and when it is deleted.
claims.quote: To assign your retention settings to content, use retention policies and retention labels with label policies. You can use just one of these methods, or combine them.

claims.where: What it is: opening paragraph and comparison table
claims.claim: Retention policies assign the same settings at container level, such as a site or mailbox.
claims.quote: A retention policy lets you do this very efficiently by assigning the same retention settings at the container level to be automatically inherited by content in that container.

claims.where: What it is: opening paragraph and comparison table
claims.claim: Retention labels assign settings at item level, including folders, documents and emails.
claims.quote: Use a retention policy to assign the same retention settings for content at a site or mailbox level, and use a retention label to assign retention settings at an item level (folder, document, email).

claims.claim: Retain-only is a supported retention outcome.
claims.quote: Retain-only: Retain content forever or for a specified period of time.

claims.claim: Delete-only is a supported retention outcome.
claims.quote: Delete-only: Permanently delete content after a specified period of time.

claims.claim: Retain and then delete is a supported retention outcome.
claims.quote: Retain and then delete: Retain content for a specified period of time and then permanently delete it.

claims.where: What it is: content stays in place
claims.claim: Content with retention settings remains in its original location.
claims.quote: When content has retention settings assigned to it, that content remains in its original location.

claims.claim: A copy is retained when retained content is edited or deleted.
claims.quote: But if they edit or delete content that's included in the retention policy, a copy of the content is automatically retained.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive retained copies use the Preservation Hold library.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive sites: The copy is retained in the Preservation Hold library.

claims.claim: Exchange mailbox retained copies use Recoverable Items.
claims.quote: For Exchange mailboxes: The copy is retained in the Recoverable Items folder.

claims.claim: Teams, Viva Engage, Copilot and AI-app retained copies use the hidden SubstrateHolds folder.
claims.quote: For Teams, Viva Engage messages, Copilot and AI apps: The copy is retained in a hidden folder named SubstrateHolds as a subfolder in the Exchange Recoverable Items folder.

claims.claim: A retention policy's settings do not travel with content moved outside its container.
claims.quote: However, the retention settings don't travel with the content in its new location. If that's required, use retention labels instead of retention policies.

claims.claim: Retention label settings travel with content moved within the Microsoft 365 tenant.
claims.quote: Unlike retention policies, retention settings from retention labels travel with the content if it's moved to a different location within your Microsoft 365 tenant.

claims.claim: Retention policy settings are not manually applied to individual items.
claims.quote: | Retention settings applied manually | No | Yes |

claims.claim: Retention labels can be applied manually.
claims.quote: Enable people in your organization to apply a retention label manually to content in Outlook and Outlook on the web, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Adaptive scope membership is determined by a daily query against selected attributes or properties.
claims.quote: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify, so the membership isn't static but dynamic by running daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected locations.

claims.claim: Static scopes cover entire locations or specific inclusions and exclusions.
claims.quote: A static scope doesn't use queries and is limited in configuration in that it can apply to all instances for a specified location, or use inclusion and exclusions for specific instances for that location.

claims.where: What it is: Precedence; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Under the ordinary retention principles, retention takes precedence over permanent deletion.
claims.quote: By default, retention always takes precedence over permanent deletion, and the longest retention period wins.

claims.claim: The longest retention period for an item wins when retention settings conflict.
claims.quote: If content is subject to multiple retention settings that retain content for different periods of time, the content is retained until the end of the longest retention period for the item.

claims.claim: A label's delete action takes precedence over a policy's delete action.
claims.quote: This means that a delete action from a retention label always takes precedence over a delete action from any retention policy.

claims.claim: For deletion conflicts between policies, adaptive or specifically included scopes take precedence over org-wide static scopes.
claims.quote: If a retention policy for a location uses an adaptive scope or a static scope that includes specific instances (such as specific users for Exchange email) that retention policy takes precedence over a static scope that is configured for all instances for the same location.

claims.claim: The shortest deletion period resolves policy deletion conflicts remaining after the preceding principles.
claims.quote: The shortest deletion period wins. Applicable to determine when items will be deleted from retention policies and the outcome couldn't be resolved from the previous level

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and AI apps
claims.claim: AI-app prompt and response data is stored for retention in a hidden folder in the app user's mailbox.
claims.quote: Data from generative AI messages is stored in a hidden folder in the mailbox of the user who runs the AI app.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and AI apps
claims.claim: An Exchange timer job evaluates AI-app data and typically takes 1-7 days to run.
claims.quote: The timer job typically takes 1-7 days to run.

claims.claim: Retaining content keeps it available for eDiscovery.
claims.quote: | Retain content | Prevent permanent deletion and remain available for eDiscovery |

claims.quote: You must set up pay-as-you-go billing to create retention policies that include the locations Microsoft Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI apps, and Other AI apps.

claims.claim: The Preservation Hold library counts towards the site's storage quota.
claims.quote: Because the Preservation Hold library is included in the site's storage quota, you might need to increase your storage when you use retention settings for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: linked archiving example
claims.claim: A feature using retention can have additional billing requirements, as with archiving retained SharePoint files.
claims.quote: To use the cost-saving benefits of Microsoft 365 Archive, first set up pay-as-you-go billing for Microsoft 365 Archive.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Retention beats deletion
claims.claim: A delete-only policy cannot permanently delete an item retained by another policy, label or eDiscovery hold.
claims.quote: Items subject to eDiscovery hold also fall under the first principle of retention; they cannot be permanently deleted by any retention policy or retention label.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Retention beats deletion
claims.claim: Retained content may disappear from users' main view while permanent deletion remains suspended.
claims.quote: the delete process can still be initiated (user-initiated or system-initiated) and consequently, might remove the content from users' main view. However, permanent deletion is suspended.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deletion is slow
claims.claim: A retention policy can take up to seven days to apply.
claims.quote: When you create and submit a retention policy, it can take up to seven days for the retention policy to be applied

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deletion is slow
claims.claim: Microsoft's AI-app example says deletion after one day could take 16 days to disappear from eDiscovery searches.
claims.quote: a delete action after 1 day could take 16 days before the message is permanently deleted so that it's no longer returned in eDiscovery searches.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Teams messages and files need separate policies
claims.claim: Teams message locations do not cover the meeting recording and transcript files.
claims.quote: Additional retention policies needed to support Teams ... This retention policy applies to content in the group's mailbox, site, and files. Files include Teams meeting recordings and transcripts from channel meetings.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Teams messages and files need separate policies
claims.claim: Meeting recordings and transcripts require the appropriate Microsoft 365 Group, SharePoint or OneDrive retention location.
claims.quote: To retain or delete Teams meeting recordings with their transcripts from user chats, you'll need a retention policy that includes the organizer's OneDrive account as the location.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Teams messages and files need separate policies
claims.claim: A file deleted by a retention policy may leave a Teams message link that returns File not found.
claims.quote: In this scenario, the file still displays in the Teams message, but when users select the file, they get a "File not found" error.

claims.quote: If you have existing retention policies for Teams chats and Copilot interactions, they continue to be supported, although they can't be edited when your tenant supports the separate locations.
